papers.title: Agent Politeness, Spatial Decision-Making, and Cognitive Load in VR
papers.meta: KTH Royal Institute of Technology · Jun 2026–Present
papers.summary: How do embodied social agents’ politeness strategies influence spatial decisions and cognitive load in VR?
papers.org:
Embodied Social Agents Lab (ESAL)
KTH Royal Institute of Technology
papers.tags:
Virtual reality
Embodied interaction
Social agents
sections: I investigate how embodied social agents’ politeness strategies influence people’s spatial decision-making and cognitive load in virtual reality.

I designed and developed a Unity-based VR experimental platform, implemented multi-stage agent requests and trial transitions, and integrated physiological recording with logs of trial events and participants’ spatial choices. I also lead experimental data collection and analysis.
Interactive prototyping in Unity; controlled user studies; behavioural and physiological measures.
First author of a methodology paper proposal submitted to HCII 2027. The full manuscript is in preparation.

papers.title: Visible Self-Repair in Conversational AI Agents
papers.meta: City University of Hong Kong · Jun–Sep 2026 · Co-first author
papers.summary: A controlled study with 60 participants exploring how visible self-repair in conversational AI affects users’ perceptions and behaviour.
papers.org:
Studio for Narrative Spaces
City University of Hong Kong
papers.tags:
Human–AI interaction
Conversational agents
User studies
sections: This project examines how visible self-repair in conversational AI agents affects users’ perceptions and behaviour. We collaboratively designed a controlled study with 60 participants.
I led study coordination and experimental sessions, built a web-based backend for interaction-log collection, and conducted the primary analysis of behavioural log data.
As co-first author, I contributed to key findings and conclusions, research figures, and the accompanying video.
The manuscript has been submitted to CHI 2027.

papers.title: Lying in Games: Exploring Prosocial Lying
papers.meta: City University of Hong Kong · Research collaboration · Sep 2026–Present
papers.summary: Exploring how prosocial lies to NPCs in Stardew Valley shape players’ perceptions and subsequent in-game behaviour.
papers.org:
In collaboration with
Studio for Narrative Spaces
City University of Hong Kong
papers.tags:
Social interaction in games
NPCs
Prosocial lying
sections: We investigate how players’ choices to tell prosocial lies to NPCs in Stardew Valley shape their perceptions and subsequent in-game behaviour.
The project examines social decisions within a game and considers potential implications for behaviour beyond the game.
I am co-authoring the manuscript as part of this ongoing research collaboration.
Work in progress. The manuscript is being prepared for a planned submission to CHI PLAY 2027.
